paragraph: [Presidential Decree 275/20 of 21 October 2020 requires private credit bureaux to keep their primary data processing centres in national territory](<https://angolex.com/paginas/decreto-presidencial/regulamento-da-actividade-das-centrais-privadas-de-informacao-de-credito.html>). Their replica sites for data recovery must also be in the country, at least 30 km from the primary centre. The decree [makes the Agência de Protecção de Dados responsible for authorising, supervising, inspecting and fining private credit bureaux](<https://angolex.com/paginas/decreto-presidencial/regulamento-da-actividade-das-centrais-privadas-de-informacao-de-credito.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No order, fine or exemption under the rule has been found, and no count of bureaux that moved data. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

On 21 October 2026 the president of Benin's data protection authority, the APDP, said that [the Code numérique requires critical servers to be sited on national territory](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2210-142651-adex-2026-mtn-benin-plaide-pour-une-cyber-resilience-proactive-a-lere-de-la-5g>). He spoke at the Africa Digital Expo in Cotonou. He called local storage a security imperative. In the last twelve months the same speech [called for rigorous application of the Code numérique](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2210-142651-adex-2026-mtn-benin-plaide-pour-une-cyber-resilience-proactive-a-lere-de-la-5g>). No earlier position has been found. No source names the body that enforces the rule. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

On 23 January 2026 Burkina Faso's Prime Minister [ordered all public platforms and data held by private hosts or abroad brought back](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/02/20/burkina-faso-zoom-sur-les-12-chantiers-strategiques-du-ministere-de-la-transition-digitale-focus-sur-le-chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-souverainete-des-donnees-via-des-datacenters-locaux/>) to two new government datacentres. The order is part of the digital ministry's programme called Zero data hosted abroad. The magazine says [the move of data still held abroad or by private hosts is to be gradual](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/02/20/burkina-faso-zoom-sur-les-12-chantiers-strategiques-du-ministere-de-la-transition-digitale-focus-sur-le-chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-souverainete-des-donnees-via-des-datacenters-locaux/>). That order is the change of the last twelve months, and no earlier rule on the state's data has been found. No body has been named to check compliance. Operating would need a body named to check compliance with the order or grant exemptions from it.

A report of November 2025 says Botswana's Data Protection Act, in effect since January 2025, [allows data to be transferred abroad only to approved countries and requires a copy of the data to remain in Botswana](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/govt-moves-to-in-house-local-data/news>). The same report says the Act was at first intended to compel businesses to store data in the country, and that the minister still intends that. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions. No order, penalty or exemption under the copy requirement has been found. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

The Ministry of Digital Transition's data governance strategy to 2030, published in 2024, [sets as a principle that all data classified as critical information infrastructure must be processed and stored inside Côte d'Ivoire](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/174196707541.pdf>). It adds that a copy of data must be kept in the country for law enforcement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No law, decree or regulation enacting the principle has been found. No body is named to enforce it. Establishing would need a rule in force that data must be kept in the country.

[In June 2025 ST Digital's chief executive said the law obliges firms in sensitive sectors to host their data in the country](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/datacenters-certifies-ecosysteme-delaisse-le-paradoxe-de-la-gouvernance-numerique-au-cameroun/>). [At Camtel's Cloud Days on 10 December 2025, speakers said the personal data protection law requires local storage](<https://lavoixdesentreprises.info/2025/12/11/digital-sovereignty-camtel-unveils-the-performance-of-its-zamengoe-datacenter-to-businesses-and-government-agencies/>). In the last twelve months the law was cited at that event and not changed, and the report names no body that enforces the storage duty. No source found gives the law's date or the wording of its duty. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

In the ministry's report of a ministerial visit on 24 July 2025, an official says [the telecommunications law requires all public administration data to be hosted in the government data centre in Kinshasa-Gombe](<https://sgptntic.gouv.cd/transition-numerique-le-ministre-augustin-kibassa-maliba-visite-le-data-center-du-gouvernement/>). The report gives no date or article for the law. It says some public data still sat on private servers at that date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions, or counts the public bodies that moved their data. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

Decree 2020-146/PR/MI, published on 13 July 2020, states in [Article 9](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/decret-n2020-146-pr-mi-portant-modalites-dacces-dexploitation-et-de-communication-du-registre-national-des-personnes-physiques/>) that the processed data of the National Register of Natural Persons are stored only on national territory. The decree governs access to, exploitation of and communication of the register. Article 9 applies to that one register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Direction Generale de la Population et de la Famille runs the register, and ANSIE is responsible for its development and security. No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

The United States government's country commercial guide of 2024 [states that data localisation is mandatory in Algeria under Law No. 18-07](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/algeria-digital-economy>), with data to be stored in the country. In November 2017 the Regulatory Authority of Post and Electronic Communications [required public cloud computing operators to build their infrastructure in Algeria and host and store their data there](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-algeria>). It issued that rule for the operators it licenses. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No order, penalty or exemption under the rule has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

The Supreme Council of Digital Society adopted Egypt's Cloud First Policy on 13 March 2024, and [it entered into force on 22 August 2024](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12346-data-localisation-requirement-in-cloud-first-policy-2024>). [It requires data classified top secret or secret to be hosted exclusively within Egypt](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12346-data-localisation-requirement-in-cloud-first-policy-2024>). The record does not say where data of lower classifications may be held, and names no date by which existing systems must move. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

No stage is set. No data localisation rule or draft has been found for Eritrea as at September 2026. No source dated in the last three years says the country has neither. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no rule that data must be kept in the country and none is being written.

[Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 entered into force on 24 July 2024](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12100-data-localisation-requirements-in-personal-data-protection-proclamation-proclamation-no-13212024>). [It requires data controllers and processors to store locally collected personal data on servers in Ethiopia](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12100-data-localisation-requirements-in-personal-data-protection-proclamation-proclamation-no-13212024>). [The Ethiopian Communications Authority's consumer rights directive of August 2021 requires telecom providers to process consumers' personal data only in Ethiopia](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-ethiopia>), and the authority issued it for the operators it licenses. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No order, penalty or exemption under these rules has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

Gabon promulgated its cybersecurity law on 11 July 2023, and [Article 27 of Law No. 027/2023 on cybersecurity and cybercrime requires data judged confidential or sensitive to be hosted exclusively on national territory](<https://journal-officiel.ga/20087-027-2023-/>). The law allows an exception: [the competent administrative authority may grant a written derogation](<https://journal-officiel.ga/20087-027-2023-/>). The text does not say which authority that is. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No derogation granted or refused has been found, and no source names an organisation ordered or penalised under the article. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

[The Bank of Ghana's Cyber and Information Security Directive of 2026 requires sensitive financial information to be stored in Ghana](<https://cioafrica.co/africa-is-arguing-with-itself/>). In the last twelve months it replaced a 2018 directive and kept core systems and critical data in the country. [The Bank of Ghana, which issued the directive, enforces it](<https://cioafrica.co/africa-is-arguing-with-itself/>), CIO Africa reports. No source found names an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the directive. No source found says whether the 2024 draft cloud framework was adopted. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

Version 2.0 of The Gambia's Government Cloud Policy, dated 29 June 2023, [says government data classed as classified shall be stored and processed within The Gambia](<https://policies.gov.gm/d/b007fc10-80d2-11ef-b086-029254d29bb1>). The Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy commissioned it. The policy says there is no law on data residence, and its issue and effective dates are blank, pending signature. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a rule in force: a law, decree, regulation or regulator's directive that data, or a named kind of data, must be kept in the country.

[Guidelines to the 2025 Kenya Cloud Policy, reported in August 2026, require top secret State data to be held in Kenya](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/corporate/technology/search-for-firm-to-host-sensitive-state-data-on-cloud-begins-5549208>). [State entities may not host data in their own server rooms without a Cloud Adoption Committee's consent](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/corporate/technology/search-for-firm-to-host-sensitive-state-data-on-cloud-begins-5549208>). In the last twelve months [A draft AI and Emerging Technologies Policy, out for comment since July 2026, would keep sensitive public datasets in Kenya](<https://cioafrica.co/ai-governance-fragmentation-cause-for-concern/>). No source found says which body checks where top secret data is held. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

A write-up of the Central Bank of Libya's Circular No. 18, which it dates 1 June 2025, says its data protection regulation [prohibits storing personal, financial, credit or sensitive data outside Libya](<https://informatics.ly/en/session/personal-data-protection-regulation-session/>). It binds banks, foreign bank branches, fintechs, payment providers, exchange companies and leasing companies from 1 July 2026. The central bank [supervises the institutions it covers and sets a fine of 100,000 dinars for each violation](<https://informatics.ly/en/session/personal-data-protection-regulation-session/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fine, revocation or exemption under the regulation has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

[Article 11 of Law No. 05-20, published on 6 August 2020, requires sensitive data to be hosted only on national territory](<https://www.anrt.ma/sites/default/files/2022-02/loi_05-20_cybersecurite_fr.pdf>). [Article 49 fines the heads of vital entities that host such data abroad 200,000 to 400,000 dirhams](<https://www.anrt.ma/sites/default/files/2022-02/loi_05-20_cybersecurite_fr.pdf>). The law text does not name the body that imposes the fines. In the last twelve months there is one new source: [A November 2026 opinion piece says the draft 2027 finance bill would store Moroccans' data in a sovereign national cloud](<https://ladsi.ma/article/tribune-souverainete-numerique-maroc-cout>). No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

A report of June 2025 on Mozambique's data governance [cites Banco de Moçambique Notice 4/GGBM/2003](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/TICID/data-governance-framework-mozambique/en_project_inception_report_mozambique_data_governance_framework.pdf>). [The notice requires data centres to be located in Mozambique, with replicas abroad allowed only with prior approval](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/TICID/data-governance-framework-mozambique/en_project_inception_report_mozambique_data_governance_framework.pdf>). The central bank issued it for the institutions it licenses, and the report records no repeal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No approval, order or penalty under the notice has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

The UN Economic Commission for Africa's 2022 digital trade regulatory profile of Malawi states that [Malawi has local storage requirements only for health-related data](<https://www.uneca.org/sites/default/files/ATPC/cp/Digital%20trade%20regulatory%20integration%20-%20Country%20profile%20-%20Malawi-%20ENG.pdf>). Its data cover 2014 to 2021, and it names no instrument for the requirement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found names a body that enforces the rule, checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

The Bank of Namibia's [Determination on Localization of Core Banking Systems (BID 19)](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2008/4109.pdf>) was signed on 5 August 2008 and took effect on 11 August 2008. It requires all authorised banking institutions to locate and maintain their core banking systems in Namibia. The Bank issued it under section 71(3) of the Banking Institutions Act 1998, and on non-compliance may pursue any remedial measure under that Act. The text refers to dispensations already granted to individual institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from the last three years names an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule. Mature would need such a dated source, or a count of those that moved data to comply.

[On 15 June 2026 the Central Bank of Nigeria ordered payment transaction data generated in Nigeria to be stored and managed there by 1 January 2027](<https://complyan.com/nigerias-cbn-data-localisation-directive-what-banks-and-fintechs-must-do-before-2027/>). [The circular binds banks, mobile money operators, switches and all licensed payment operators](<https://complyan.com/nigerias-cbn-data-localisation-directive-what-banks-and-fintechs-must-do-before-2027/>). In the last twelve months it is new, and no earlier central bank rule on payment data has been found. The bank [says it will monitor compliance and may impose supervisory sanctions, though the circular sets no penalty schedule](<https://thetrumpet.ng/cbn-insists-on-january-1-2027-deadline-for-banks-fintechs-to-store-payment-data-in-nigeria/>). In October 2026 a NITDA survey found 22 of 44 institutions yet to begin. No organisation has been named as ordered, penalised or exempted. Mature would need such a named organisation, or a count of those that moved data.

A market brief of July 2025 says [there is no blanket localisation requirement in Rwanda, but some data must be stored locally depending on the circumstances](<https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Digital-Investment-Facility/2507_Country-Market-Briefs/Data-Center-Market-Brief-Rwanda.pdf>). Public sector data must be hosted in the government data centre or in facilities meeting Rwanda Development Board standards. In May 2017 the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority [fined MTN Rwanda FRW 7.03 billion for hosting its IT services outside the country](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-rwanda>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No order, penalty or certificate from the last three years has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

A study by the Sudanese Center for Policy Studies of 19 July 2026 says [mobile banking data transits infrastructure Sudan neither owns nor regulates, with no statutory requirement governing data localisation or cross-border transfer](<https://sudancps.com/en/2026/07/19/sudans-privacy-gap-balancing-digital-transformation-and-data-laws-intro/>). It proposes localisation as a first piece of legislation and reports no drafting. An article of October 2023 [states that Sudan has no law imposing data localisation](<https://advox.globalvoices.org/2023/10/21/the-ongoing-conflicts-impact-on-ict-and-digital-transformation-efforts-in-sudan/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No newer source says a rule is being written. Preparing would need a rule that data must be stored or processed in the country to be written or out for consultation.

An account of September 2025 says President Macky Sall, after the Diamniadio National Datacenter opened in June 2021, [told his government to migrate all state data and platforms to it](<https://africachinainitiative.georgetown.edu/research-working-group/blog-posts/huawei-helping-or-hindering-african-countries-secure-their-data-sovereignty-2/>). He also told it to bring home national data hosted abroad. The account names no legal instrument. In December 2024 the health ministry [was carrying a draft digital health law and decree that cover hosting health data in Senegal](<https://www.enda-sante.org/letat-du-senegal-entre-transformation-numerique-et-renforcement-de-la-legislation/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body that checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

A ministerial order of 27 August 2025 [requires Starlink to keep its users' connection logs, IP addresses and traffic data for at least 24 months](<https://ecomatin.net/telecoms-ndjamena-accentue-la-pression-sur-airtel-moov-et-starlink>). [The data must be hosted in Chad and open to the national authorities](<https://ecomatin.net/telecoms-ndjamena-accentue-la-pression-sur-airtel-moov-et-starlink>), EcoMatin reports. Breach can bring [fines, suspension or withdrawal of Starlink's licence](<https://ecomatin.net/telecoms-ndjamena-accentue-la-pression-sur-airtel-moov-et-starlink>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The telecommunications minister issued the order, and it names no body to check where the data are kept. Operating would need a body named to check where the data are kept or to grant exemptions.

[Article 21 of decree-law 2022-2 of 4 January 2022 bars credit information companies from transferring their databases outside Tunisia](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-loi-n-2022-2-du-4-janvier-2022-portant-organisation-de-lactivite-du-renseignement-de-credit/>), or from setting up sites outside the country to protect the data given to them. Under the decree-law [the Banque centrale de Tunisie licenses credit information companies](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-loi-n-2022-2-du-4-janvier-2022-portant-organisation-de-lactivite-du-renseignement-de-credit/>). [Its governor may fine one 10,000 to 50,000 dinars](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-loi-n-2022-2-du-4-janvier-2022-portant-organisation-de-lactivite-du-renseignement-de-credit/>), suspend its activity for three months or withdraw its licence. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fine, suspension or withdrawal for keeping data abroad has been found. Mature would need a dated source naming a company ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

The Cybercrimes (Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure) Order of 19 June 2026 [requires owners of critical information infrastructure to host all related data inside the country](<https://media.tanzlii.org/media/legislation/400769/source_file/b94ac284c6b6b841/cybercrimes-protection-of-critical-information-infrastructure-order-2026.pdf>). Hosting data abroad needs the Minister's approval. The ICT ministry keeps the register and audits the infrastructure. The Bank of Tanzania's Cloud Computing Guidelines of August 2025 [bar licensed financial providers from hosting mission-critical systems in a data centre or cloud outside Tanzania](<https://www.bot.go.tz/webdocs/Feedback/en/2025082512452979.pdf>). In the last twelve months the Order is new, and no earlier rule for critical infrastructure has been found. No approval, refusal or penalty under either rule is on record. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted, or a count of those that moved data.

South Africa's rule covers government data on national security. [The communications department told Parliament on 24 February 2026](<http://www.ellipsis.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/260224_PCCDT_presentation_-_Data_Centres.pdf>) that, under the National Data and Cloud Policy, such data shall be stored only in infrastructure inside the country. [A draft commented on in 2021](<https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/digital-sovereignty-in-the-brics-countries/south-african-digital-sovereignty-at-the-crossroad-of-securitization-and-development/08C1119DE09286B84626FA49F6AD0586>) went further and required a copy of data to be kept in the country. No change to the rule has been found in the last twelve months. No body has been found that checks compliance or grants exemptions. Operating would need a body named to enforce the rule.

A D4D Hub research paper states that [Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 requires sensitive personal data](<https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Data-Policies-and-Regulations/Examining-Sensitive-Personal-Data-Protection-and-Data-Sovereignty-in-Zambia.pdf>) to be stored within the country. The paper quotes Section 70: sensitive personal data can only be stored in Zambia. It says the Data Protection Commission, established in 2023, enforces the Act and holds the power to approve transfers abroad. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from the last three years names an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule. Mature would need such a dated source, or a count of those that moved data to comply.

The regulator POTRAZ, as Zimbabwe's designated Data Protection Authority, published implementation guidelines for the Cyber and Data Protection Act in 2025. [It states that it will not permit highly sensitive information such as core banking platforms and critical financial systems to be hosted outside Zimbabwe](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/Cyber%20and%20Data%20Protection%20Act%20Implementation%20Guidlines.pdf>). The guidelines [name POTRAZ as the body whose prior written approval is required for any exception to local hosting](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/Cyber%20and%20Data%20Protection%20Act%20Implementation%20Guidlines.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No approval granted or refused has been found, and no organisation ordered or penalised. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.
